verdict.root_cause: Two minutes before onset, platform-automation set QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR on shippingservice to an address naming an absent quote host [tr_4891b42b3bd9]. From onset shippingservice still logs every inbound GetQuote but never emits the paired quote-sent line or any ship-order activity, with no error-level output at all [tr_253b1eca761e] — it can no longer produce a quote. checkoutservice consequently fails on exactly one hop: its client span for ShippingService/GetQuote is ERROR in every failing post-15:21:30 trace, and PlaceOrder aborts inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart before payment, email or ShipOrder are attempted [tr_5a04b0440243], matching checkout logs where post-onset order lines lack all follow-on entries [tr_728eaeaa1680]. checkoutservice and frontend only noticed; the wrong value on shippingservice is the mechanism.
verdict.reasoning: The only change in effect at onset is the env edit landing ~2 minutes prior, unreverted unlike its two earlier applications; both image changes were reverted ~3.3h earlier [tr_4891b42b3bd9], and shipping shows no startup/config-load failure or restart [tr_253b1eca761e], which excludes bad_deploy. Traces localise the error to the GetQuote hop with cart, catalog and currency healthy in the same traces [tr_5a04b0440243]. The failure mode is error, not wait — failing traces are 8-20ms with 2.5-4.3ms GetQuote spans [tr_5a04b0440243] — excluding dependency_latency. checkout has no change of its own to roll back [tr_ee62daef3e7d] and its error elevation is episodic, not a monotonic ramp [tr_75c73d19dc55], excluding exhaustion. The value is wrong in itself and its wrongness breaks the request, so reverting QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR (and stopping the automation loop re-applying it) is the fix.
open_questions: No evidence directly observes shippingservice failing to reach the configured host — no connection/DNS error line, and the downstream http-client span is not marked ERROR [tr_5a04b0440243]; the link is inferred from timing and log shape.
shippingservice has no call-count or error-ratio samples in either window [tr_479f55d42c39], so its request rate, restarts and readiness are unmeasured and its metric pipeline may itself be broken.
checkout logs are truncated across the onset minute [tr_728eaeaa1680], and the automation loop may re-revert the value on its own as it did twice before [tr_4891b42b3bd9], masking the fix.

alternatives.root_cause: The quote backend shippingservice depends on is independently down, and shipping fails waiting on or failing over to it.
alternatives.why_not: Failing traces are 8-20ms with healthy-duration GetQuote spans [tr_5a04b0440243], so nothing is waiting; and the address in effect at onset itself names an absent host [tr_4891b42b3bd9].

alternatives.root_cause: shippingservice is running a wrong artifact from the earlier adservice-tagged image changes, breaking quote generation.
alternatives.why_not: Both image changes were reverted ~3.3h before onset so the baseline image was live [tr_4891b42b3bd9], and no startup or init failure appears in the logs [tr_253b1eca761e].

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring shippingservice's pre-15:19:07 environment (QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR unset, i.e. the state before the platform-automation edit) and recreating the container should make GetQuote complete again. Observable, in this order: (1) shipping-service Loki stream resumes the pre-onset shape — each inbound 'GetQuoteRequest' INFO line followed within milliseconds by a quote-sent line, and ship-order/tracking-ID lines reappear; (2) in Tempo, the checkoutservice client span for ShippingService/GetQuote stops being marked ERROR in new traces, and PlaceOrder traces once again carry payment, email, EmptyCart and ShipOrder children instead of terminating inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart; (3) checkout-service logs resume the payment / confirmation-email / message-write entries after each order-placement line; (4) checkoutservice error ratio (calls_total STATUS_CODE_ERROR / calls_total, 2m) falls back toward its ~0.03 baseline. Note that shippingservice's own error-ratio series is empty in both windows, so confirmation must come from shipping logs and checkout traces, not from shippingservice metrics.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, more than ~2 minutes after the recreate, shipping-service still logs inbound GetQuote lines with no paired quote-sent line, or checkoutservice client spans for ShippingService/GetQuote are still ERROR in traces started after the recreate. Also treat as not-confirmed if the change log shows platform-automation re-applying QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR=http://quoteservice-gone:8090 within the confirmation window — it did exactly this twice earlier in the day, so a recurrence would mask or undo the fix and the real remedy (stopping the automation loop) is outside this system's permitted actions. A third falsifier: the prior configuration had QUOTE_SERVICE_ADDR absent entirely, so if shippingservice needs some quote address to serve quotes, reverting to 'unset' may leave it equally unable to complete — visible as unchanged log shape after recreate.
proposal.risk: The causal link is inferred, not observed: no connection or DNS error line exists on shippingservice and the downstream http-client span is not marked ERROR [tr_5a04b0440243], so the bad address may not be the mechanism. If so, this recreate discards the failing process state — the one thing that could still be inspected — without fixing anything, and makes the next diagnosis harder. The recreate itself resets shippingservice's in-process cache and drops any in-flight GetQuote/ShipOrder calls, producing a short burst of additional checkout failures on top of the current ones. If the previous configuration is itself incomplete (the recorded prior value is None), reverting could leave shippingservice with a default target that is also unreachable, converting a known-bad state into an unclear one. Finally, shippingservice's metric series is empty [tr_479f55d42c39], so if log evidence is also ambiguous after the revert we will have no independent signal that the service is healthy.
proposal.blast_radius: One service is changed: shippingservice. During the recreate its callers see connection resets — checkoutservice directly (GetQuote and ShipOrder), and through it frontend and loadgenerator, whose PlaceOrder requests are already failing. The reverted value is a dependency address, so the host named by the bad value (quoteservice-gone:8090) stops receiving attempts and whatever the prior configuration resolves to begins receiving them. No other service in the incident's blast radius is touched; checkoutservice has no recorded change and is not modified [tr_ee62daef3e7d].

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts starting at checkoutservice and propagating to frontend and the load generator describe a user-facing checkout failure that cannot be dismissed, and no open incident covers it. The alert pattern alone does not distinguish a bad deploy of checkoutservice from a failing downstream dependency, so the fault class stays unknown.
